'''Justus Akinbayo Akinsanya''', [[Royal College of Nursing|FRCN]] (31 December 1936 &ndash; 11 August 2005) was a [[nurse]], [[Human biology|human biologist]], [[Nurse Educator|nurse educator]] and [[research]]er.

==Early life and career==
Born in [[Okun-Owa]], [[Ijebu (province)|Ijebu]], [[Nigeria]] (near [[Lagos]]) in 1936 he came to the [[United Kingdom]] aged 21.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |date=1987-11-14 |title=Equal Justus: As a high-ranking black nurse, Justus Akinsanya uses his status to battle against racism in the profession. He talks to Jane Salvage |url=http://journals.rcni.com/doi/10.7748/ns.2.7.32.s66 |journal=Nursing Standard |language=en |volume=2 |issue=7 |pages=32 |doi=10.7748/ns.2.7.32.s66 |issn=0029-6570|url-access=subscription }}</ref>  He started his career in nursing at Abergele Chest Hospital in Wales 1958-1959<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Akinsanya |first=Justus |date=13 Jul 1972 |title=Talking to the Students |journal=Nursing Times |volume=68 |issue=28}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> where he qualified as a registered fever nurse (gaining a Tuberculosis Association Certificate).<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Akinsanya; Justus Akinbayo (1936-2005); nurse professor |url=https://rcn.epexio.com/names/f6b41c24-d58c-ff93-5527-e2b75091e71b |access-date=2024-11-19 |website=RCN Archive Catalogue |language=en-gb}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |title=General Register of Nurses |date=1961–1962 |publisher=General Nursing Council for England and Wales }}</ref>

Akinsanya then trained in General Nursing at Crumpsall Hospital, Manchester 1959-1962.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Johnson |first=David |date=2005-09-07 |title=Justus Akinsanya will long be remembered |url=http://journals.rcni.com/doi/10.7748/ns.19.52.39.s56 |journal=Nursing Standard |language=en |volume=19 |issue=52 |pages=39 |doi=10.7748/ns.19.52.39.s56 |issn=0029-6570|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 1967 he did post-registration courses in [[orthopaedic|orthopaedics]]  at Lord Mayor Treloar Hospital in Hampshire,  [[dermatological|dermatology]]  at St. John's Hospital for Diseases of the Skin in London and [[psychiatric]] nursing.<ref name=":1" />

From 1964-1969 he held charge nurse's posts in Essex, Bristol and Bath, before entering the [[Borough Polytechnic]] in London to take the Sister Tutors' Diploma course.<ref name=":1" /> By 1972<ref name=":1" /> he entered the [[University of London]] where he obtained a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc (Hons)]] degree in Human Biology. He subsequently found it difficult to find work as a graduate Nurse Tutor, mainly because of the profession's wariness of graduate nurses. [[Peggy Nuttall]] of the [[Nursing Times]], persuaded him to write an article, ''Wanted Tutors: graduates need not apply'',<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Dopson |first=Laurence |date=5 December 2005 |title=Justus Akinsanya Nurse educationist and pioneer of 'bio-nursing' |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/justus-akinsanya-518170.html |access-date=25 November 2024 |work=The Independent}}</ref> one of many articles that Akinsanya was to write, but one that was written under the pseudonym of J Jones Subiar.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Subiar |first=J Jones |date=9 Aug 1973 |title=Wanted: Nurse Tutors … Graduates Need Not Apply |journal=Nursing Times |volume=69 |issue=32|pmid=4727575 }}</ref>   As a result he was offered a tutor's job at King's College Hospital, London.<ref name=":3" /> He went on to hold positions as a teacher, administrator and researcher.<ref name=":2" />

He then returned to Nigeria for a few years where he worked for the [[Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria]] (Education)<ref name=":0" /> as Deputy Secretary/Acting Registrar 1977-1978<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite journal |date=23 Feb 1978 |title=The Commonwealth Scene |journal=Nursing Times |volume=74 |issue=8}}</ref> where he set up writers’ workshops for professional nurses in Nigeria in 1977.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Akinsanya |first=Justus |date=23 Feb 1978 |title=Nursing Council of Nigeria, Follow-Up Report |journal=Nursing Times |volume=74 |issue=8}}</ref>  He was a lecturer at the Institute of Management and Technology in [[Enugu (city)|Enugu]] 1976-1977.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Akinsanya |first=Justus A. |date=3 Mar 1977 |title=Preaching What You Practise |journal=Nursing Times |volume=73 |issue=9}}</ref>

He returned to the UK and gained a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] at [[King's College London]] for his thesis ''Knowledge of the life sciences as a basis for practice: some problems in nurse education'' awarded in 1984<ref>{{Cite web |title=Knowledge of the life sciences as a basis for practice : some problems in nurse education. |url=https://kclpure.kcl.ac.uk/portal/en/studentTheses/knowledge-of-the-life-sciences-as-a-basis-for-practice-some-probl |access-date=2024-11-19 |website=King's College London |language=en}}</ref>  This explored his influential concept of bio-nursing, which he defined as clinical nursing that uses in practice the principles of natural sciences such as biology.<ref>{{cite web|title=Professor Justus A Akinsanya|work=Royal College of Nursing, Fellows|url=http://www.rcn.org.uk/aboutus/fellows/akinsanya.php|archive-url=https://archive.today/20071022195852/http://www.rcn.org.uk/aboutus/fellows/akinsanya.php|url-status=dead|archive-date=2007-10-22|accessdate=2006-10-20}}</ref>

From 1985-1989 he was at the [[Dorset Institute of Higher Education]], first as Reader<ref name=":0" /> and later Professor and Head of the Health Care Research Unit, making him one of the early nurse-professors.<ref name=":3" />  Whilst there he published his influential biography ''An African 'Florence Nightingale': A biography of Chief (Dr.) Mrs. [[Kofoworola Abeni Pratt]]'' (Vantage, 1987).<ref>{{Cite book |last=Akinsanya |first=Justus A. |title=An African 'Florence Nightingale': a biography of Chief (Dr.) Mrs. Kofoworola Abeni Pratt |date=1987 |publisher=Vantage Publishers |isbn=978-978-2458-26-1 |location=Ibadan, Nigeria}}</ref>

He subsequently took up the post of Academic Dean and Pro-Vice Chancellor of the newly created Faculty of Health and Social Work at [[Anglia Polytechnic University]] 1989-1996,<ref name=":3" /> where his wife, Cynthia Marcelle,<ref name=":3" /> worked as a lecturer in pre-registration nursing.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Akinsanya|first1=Justus|last2=Akinsanya|first2=Justus A|date=1990-10-31|title=Future hiding in the present|journal=Nursing Standard|volume=5|issue=6|pages=13–15|doi=10.7748/ns.5.6.13.s69|pmid=2124890|issn=0029-6570}}</ref>

Akinsanya highlighted racial injustice through his work for the [[Commission for Racial Equality]] and the [[Royal College of Nursing]] (RCN)<ref name=":0" /> He persuaded the Commission for Racial Equality to fund a study, and was shocked to discover widespread racism in the National Health Service. On discovering the only reports were on doctors, he researched and self published his work ''Ethnic minority nurses, midwives and health visitors what role for them in the National Health Service?'' (Self published, London 1986)<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite book |last=Akinsanya |first=Justus Akinbayo |title=Ethnic minority nurses, midwives and health visitors what role for them in the National Health Service? |publisher=Self published |year=1986 |location=London}}</ref>  He also sat on the RCN working party on nursing in a multiracial society<ref name=":0" /> and he was the first black member of the English National Board for Nursing, Midwifery and Health Visiting 1988 -1993.<ref name=":3" />

In 1991, Akinsanya published the results of a major national study of attitudes of nurses and their teachers to Aids he had carried out in ''Who Will Care? a survey of the knowledge and attitudes of hospital nurses to people with HIV/AIDS: report submitted to the Department of Health (Anglia Polytechnic, Chelmsford 1991)''<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":2" />

He was made an Emeritus Professor by the Dorset Institute upon his retirement in 1996,<ref name=":2" /> and then devoted his time to the charitable activities of Disability Croydon, Nurses Fund for Nurses and the [[Nigerian]] Council of Elders, and served as a local education authority (LEA) governor of two schools in [[Croydon]].<ref name=":2" />

==Personal life==
He had been involved in the [[Nursing Council of Nigeria]] and he was made a fellow of the UK [[Royal College of Nursing]] (FRCN) in 1988.<ref>{{Cite web |title=RCN Fellows and Honorary Fellows |url=https://www.rcn.org.uk/About-us/RCN-Fellows-and-Honorary-Fellows |access-date=7 Nov 2022 |website=Royal College of Nursing}}</ref>

==Death==
He died in [[London]] at the age of 68 after contracting an infection at the [[International Council of Nurses]] conference in [[Taiwan]] some months earlier.
